Each CTA processes just 128 elements (1 load + 3 strided scatter stores) and terminates almost immediately, leaving 66.75% of scheduler slots empty. The dominant stall is L1TEX scoreboard (43.9% of cycles, 13.9 cycles avg) from the three non-unit-stride stores (×448, ×480, ×512). Prior attempts to fix this via @triton.autotune with XBLOCK as a constexpr all crashed with 'RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]' — a JIT binary loading failure caused by incorrect autotune usage with tl.constexpr parameters. The correct fix is a persistent kernel: keep XBLOCK=128 as a fixed constexpr (avoiding the JIT crash), launch exactly num_sms CTAs (132), and have each CTA loop over ceil(xnumel / (XBLOCK * num_sms)) tiles. This gives each CTA ~15x more work (1960/132 ≈ 14.8 tiles per CTA), dramatically increasing in-flight memory operations per CTA and hiding the L1TEX latency through ILP across tile iterations.
